subject: MSA + Order Form - Indemnity scope & evidence obligations
messages:
From: Evan Li <evan.li@hightide.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Hightide Procurement <procurement@hightide.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redlines: indemnity scope and evidence asks

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We reviewed the MSA + Order Form and have a few open items on the indemnity section we need to resolve before procurement can sign off. High-level asks:

- Defense control: your redline currently reserves Redwood the right to "control defense" for 3P IP claims. We need clarity on whether customer can take over defense and what limits apply (cost caps, counsel approval).
- Evidence and notice: procurement wants a concrete list of technical evidence Redwood needs to investigate an alleged infringement (logs, content samples, model version + prompt history). Can you confirm minimum evidence and retention window?
- AI output carveouts: we flagged scenarios where output is derivative of customer-provided copyrighted material or clearly user-supplied content — that should shift responsibility.
- Reimbursement vs. defend-and-indemnify: if Redwood defends and loses, what is the reimbursable bucket vs. third-party settlement approvals?

Attached are our redlines (Hightide_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf). Can we get Redwood's counterproposal by early next week? If easier, we can do a 30-minute call Thu/Fri.

Thanks,
Evan

--
Evan Li
Head of Procurement, Hightide AI
procurement@hightide.ai

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@hightide.ai>
Cc: Hightide Procurement <procurement@hightide.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines: indemnity scope and evidence asks

Evan —

Appreciate the clear notes and the redlines. We've reviewed and sketched a pragmatic compromise that preserves buyer protections while keeping operational burden reasonable for both sides. Quick summary up front:

1) Defense control: Redwood can offer a right to defend for third-party IP claims (typical "right to control" language) but we are willing to add a step where Customer may assume defense if Redwood doesn't commence within 30 days or if Customer reasonably requests it. If Customer takes control, Redwood requests approval rights over counsel and reasonable joint-defense cooperation terms.

2) Evidence & notice: we'll commit to a minimum evidence checklist (model id + hash, prompt transcript, output sample, ingestion timestamps, and relevant KV/log snapshots). We propose a 90-day retention baseline for prompt/output artifacts tied to the purchase order; longer retention can be added under a data addendum.

3) AI output carveouts: where Customer can demonstrate (preponderance) that the alleged infringement is traceable to Customer-supplied content or an exact copy of a Customer-provided file, responsibility shifts to Customer. For ambiguous cases we propose joint triage with an independent technical reviewer.

4) Reimbursement buckets: if Redwood controls defense we cover settlements and judgments; if Customer controls defense we are open to a negotiated reimbursement cap and approval rights for settlements affecting Redwood.

I'll loop in Kimberly (legal) for precise contract language and Ben (ops) for the evidence/retention feasibility.

Are you available for a 30-minute sync Fri 6/20 at 10am PT? If not, suggest a time. We'll attach a redline with the proposed MSA paragraph and an evidence checklist.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Hightide indemnity questions & proposed language (please draft)

Kimberly / Ben —

Forwarding Evan's note and our quick summary. Can you two help by drafting the contract-ready language and a one-page ops evidence checklist we can send to procurement? Key items we need to nail down:

- Precise MSA paragraph for "Right to Defend" with 30-day cure window and Customer-assume path, plus explicit cooperation obligations (privilege-preserving info exchange).
- A short definition of "Customer-provided content" that is narrow but testable (checksums / file IDs / upload timestamps).
- Evidence minimums: model name/version, model artifact hash, prompt transcript (last 1k tokens), sample outputs, ingestion logs for the 48-hour window around the reported event, and any matching customer files.
- Retention: confirm whether 90 days is operationally feasible or whether we need a different baseline. If 90d is OK, Ben: please flag any cost impact for the customer's account class (S, M, L).

I attached a starter spreadsheet (indemnity_evidence_checklist.xlsx) with a suggested column layout (evidence, who produces it, estimated time-to-produce).

Kimberly: draft conservative language but include an inline comment about the reimbursement cap option if Customer assumes control. Ben: note expected time to gather artifacts and whether any special telemetry flags are required.

Thanks — target to have draft outbound by EOD Thu so we have time to iterate before Friday's sync.

Grace

[Attachment: indemnity_evidence_checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Evan Li <evan.li@hightide.ai>
Cc: Hightide Procurement <procurement@hightide.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: MSA redlines: indemnity scope and evidence asks

Evan —

Thanks for the patience while we ran this through legal and ops. Attached is a concise counterproposal and an operations checklist to make triage predictable. Highlights:

- Defense control: Redwood retains the right to control the defense for third-party claims alleging IP infringement of a third party. If Redwood does not commence a defense within 30 days of receiving a valid notice, Customer may assume defense. If Customer assumes defense, Redwood will reasonably cooperate and will have the right to approve lead counsel if Customer's chosen counsel would materially prejudice Redwood.

- Evidence & retention: minimum evidence required is: (i) model identifier + artifact hash; (ii) prompt transcript and output sample; (iii) ingestion/event timestamps and relevant request ids; (iv) matching customer file identifiers where applicable. Redwood will maintain full artifacts for 90 days by default. If Hightide requires longer retention we can attach a paid data-retention addendum to the Order Form.

- Carveouts and triage: where Customer demonstrates the output is substantially derived from Customer-provided content (checksum match, exact text match, or explicit upload provenance), Customer responsibility applies. For disputes on provenance, we propose an independent technical reviewer to arbitrate for the first 2 claims per 12-month period; additional reviews can be agreed with a cost split.

- Settlements and reimbursement: when Redwood controls the defense we cover judgments and settlements. If Customer controls defense we will discuss a capped reimbursement path and require notice & prior approval for any settlement that would impose ongoing product restrictions on Redwood.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached redline (Hightide_MSA_v3_redlines.pdf) and the evidence checklist (indemnity_evidence_checklist.xlsx).
- If acceptable in principle, I can route this to DocuSign for the Order Form addendum and loop in our procurement lead to finalize the PO terms. DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abcdef

Happy to hop on a call if you prefer to walk through the changes — we have a 30-min slot Mon 6/23 at 11am PT.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
